messages:
Maya: Quick idea — add a "Compare mode" in Console analytics so you can view per-route vs per-model side-by-side, with quota overlays and a way to pin time slices. Thoughts?
Sam: Love it. Is the default scope route or model?
Maya: Default to route context (so you see metrics for the route you clicked), with a toggle to switch to model-scoped view (aggregate across routes using that model). Compare mode lets you pick two axes: e.g., baseline vs canary model version, or two time windows.
Leo: Need quota-awareness: show remaining quota as a shaded band on token charts and flag routes that are close to throttling. Saved queries should also indicate if they reference route-scoped metrics vs org-scoped quotas.
Ana: UX idea: top context bar with pills — [Route: /v1/generate] [Model: redwood-v1] [Time: last 6h] then a "Compare" button that opens a lightweight drawer for selecting the second axis (model version / time shift / percentile). Saved query modal should have a checkbox: "Save scope with query" (inherit vs pin-to-route).
Ryan: Edge case — teams often want the same saved query applied across different routes. If "pin-to-route" is default we risk fragmentation. Maybe default to "inherit scope" and surface a small "pin" CTA.
Maya: Proposed saved query schema (very rough):
```json
{
  "name": "latency-by-model",
  "owner": "team:platform",
  "visibility": "team", // personal | team | org
  "scope": "inherit", // inherit | route:/v1/generate | model:redwood-v1
  "compareMode": true,
  "compareSpec": {"type":"model_version","left":"redwood-v1","right":"redwood-v1-canary"},
  "timeRange": "last_6h",
  "filters": ["status:5xx","model:startswith:redwood"],
  "pinnedSnapshotId": null
}
```
Sam: How do we handle naming conflicts? If two saved queries have same name in the same visibility we should warn and suggest suffixes (or auto-append owner).
Leo: Telemetry notes — track: compare_mode_used, compare_type, saved_query_scope, snapshot_taken. This will help us pick defaults (e.g., if >50% users compare by model version make that primary). Also record sampling rate for heavy routes to avoid blowing up metrics backend.
Ana: Perf: per-route + per-model cross joins can be expensive. Lazy-load the full model list, show a condensed "model summary" row with aggregated metrics, and let users expand to full per-model rows. Also support server-side snapshots for extremely heavy queries.
Maya: Rollout UX — allow selecting two model versions to overlay latency/error percentiles and request volume. Keep the selection in the URL so teams can share comparisons in tickets.
Ryan: Implementation question: saved queries materialized or computed on-demand? My take: compute on-demand normally; offer a "snapshot now" action that materializes results for heavy queries or for point-in-time comparisons. Snapshots can be small time-bucket exports stored for 90 days.
Sam: +1 for "snapshot now". Also add a small CTA in the saved-query list: "last run" and size estimate so users know cost before running.
console-bot: deploy scheduled: analytics-backend v3.4 deployed to staging. Please smoke test compare mode in /staging.
Ana: I'll mock up the context bar + compare drawer in Figma and post a link later today.
Maya: Great — I'll file a roadmap ticket and open a small PR for the saved-query schema changes. @Sam can you own the conflict UX?
Sam: Yep, I'll take it. @Maya lgtm. :thumbsup:
Leo: Also, can we add a lightweight warning when a saved query's scope will cause quota-related anomalies? e.g., "This query includes org-level quota metrics; results may differ when run with route scope."
Maya: Good call. Add to the UX notes.
Ana: Sharing initial Figma: https://figma.com/s/example-compare-mode (prototype in progress)
Maya: Thanks — will iterate after the prototype.
